Q1: Which branch should the fixture fix be committed to?
Choices:
A) PR #6574's head branch `ai/issue-6570`. Add the commit there, for example through that PR's review/autofix loop, so its CI turns green before merge. (RECOMMENDED)
B) The default branch `main`, after PR #6574 has merged. Hold this issue until then and fix the fixture on `main` as a follow-up.
C) Neither. Close this issue and let PR #6574's own review/autofix pass, which already sees the failed `CI` check-run, apply the fix.
Q2: How far should the test hardening go?
Choices:
A) Only what the triage proposes: add `--no-local` to the `work` clone in `_git_fixture`, and assert the older commit is absent immediately after fixture setup. Do not change `scripts/review_merge_train.sh`. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Option A, plus extend the absence check to every test that uses the fixture, not just the two that fail.
